# EvInputFieldUnit

> A composite input pairing a leading unit selector (dropdown) with a text/number field. Use it for values that carry a unit — e.g. amount + currency, weight + unit. It supports validation and the same interaction states as InputField.

| ID | `evoq-ui:input-field-unit` |
| Layer | Molecule (`src/molecules`) |

| Extra attributes go to | the inner `<EvInput>`, not the root |

  placeholder="0"
  label="Nilai kontrak"
/>

## Design guidance

From the Figma page **Input**, frame `4707:9944` (InputFieldUnit). These rules are binding. Names in them are Figma's - the Vue API is the tables above.

### When to use

- Use for a value plus a selectable unit (e.g. 10 + kg, 100 + USD).
- Use the leading dropdown to choose the unit.
- Use the field for the numeric/text value.
- Use validation text to guide correction inline.
- Use the disabled state when the value is not editable.

### When not to use

- Don't use when there is no unit  →  use InputField (`evoq-ui:input`).
- Don't use for choosing only from a set  →  use InputDropdown.
- Don't put the unit inside the value field as text.
- Don't hide which part is editable.

### Do

- Keep the unit list short and relevant.
- Align the dropdown and field heights.
- Show validation text close to the field, on error.
- Default the unit to the most common choice.

### Don't

- Rely on the placeholder alone as the label.
- Use red borders without an explanatory message.
- Mix unrelated units in one selector.
- Disable a field without making the reason clear.

## Contract

- Only the props, slots and events above exist on `EvInputFieldUnit`; anything not listed is not part of its API.
- An attribute that is not a prop (`class`, `id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`) goes to the inner `<EvInput>`, not the root.
- Import it by name from `evoq-ui`; styles come once from `evoq-ui/style.css`.
- Refer to it by id `evoq-ui:input-field-unit` - the id stays the same if the component moves layer.
